aggressive_definition: T3 and T4 prostate cancers were analyzed as extent-defined aggressive disease categories; T3 extends through the prostate capsule, while T4 is fixed or invades adjacent structures.
aggressive_definition_excerpt: The present secondary analysis is based on the aforementioned nested case-control study of prostate cancer [ 5 ] that included 71 cases diagnosed with T2 primary cancer (tumor confined within the prostate), 51 cases with T3 (tumor extends through the prostate capsule), and 15 cases with T4 (tumor is fixed or invades adjacent structures other than seminal vesicles, such as external sphincter, rectum, bladder, levator muscles and/or pelvic wall) [ 53 ].
study_design: Prospective nested case-control analysis within the ATBC Study cohort
cohort_total_n_excerpt: To elucidate whether those metabolomic profiles represent etiologic or tumor biomarker signals, we prospectively examined serum metabolites of prostate cancer cases by size and extent of primary tumors in a nested case-control analysis in the ATBC Study cohort that compared cases diagnosed with T2 (n = 71), T3 (n = 51), or T4 (n = 15) disease to controls (n = 200).
reason: Prediagnostic serum metabolites were prospectively evaluated for incident T2, T3, and T4 cancers separately. T3 and T4 constitute aggressive extent-defined endpoints, but the abstract does not present an overall or total prostate cancer analysis; therefore the article is aggressive_only rather than both.
